stories.headline: QC Court Issues Arrest Warrant Against VP Sara Duterte in Grave Threats Case
stories.deck: Vice President Sara Duterte’s lawyer confirmed that a Quezon City court issued a warrant of arrest in the grave threats case. A DOJ source separately confirmed the issuance to GMA News.
body: A Quezon City court has issued a warrant of arrest against Vice President Sara Duterte in connection with the grave threats case filed against her, according to her lawyer Paul Lawrence Lim on Friday, September 4.

The Department of Justice filed three counts of grave threats in August over Duterte’s November 2024 remarks involving President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
The warrant adds a separate criminal proceeding to the vice president’s already consequential legal and political situation while her impeachment trial continues before the Senate.
Watch for the warrant’s service, any posting of bail, and further orders from the Quezon City court on Duterte’s pending jurisdictional challenge and motion to quash.

stories.headline: Marcos Administration Proposes ₱197.3 Billion for Rail Transport in 2027
stories.deck: The proposal would more than triple 2026 rail funding and concentrate most of the allocation on the North-South Commuter Railway and Metro Manila Subway.
body: The Marcos administration proposed ₱197.3 billion for the rail transport program under the 2027 National Expenditure Program, more than triple the amount provided under the 2026 General Appropriations Act.

About ₱191.28 billion, nearly 97 percent of the proposed rail budget, is earmarked for two flagship projects: ₱123.84 billion for the North-South Commuter Railway and ₱67.44 billion for Phase I of the Metro Manila Subway.
The proposal also includes funding for the LRT-1 Cavite Extension, MRT-3 rehabilitation and interim operations related to the common-station connection among major rail lines.
The amount is an executive budget proposal and remains subject to congressional scrutiny, amendment and approval.

stories.headline: Marcos Signs Law Expanding Tertiary Education Aid for Poorer Students
stories.deck: Republic Act No. 12325 strengthens the country’s free tertiary education framework by giving poor and disadvantaged learners greater priority in government assistance and expanding support pathways for eligible college and technical-vocational students.
body: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Republic Act No. 12325 at Malacañang on Friday, September 4, amending the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act of 2017.

Republic Act No. 10931 established free tuition and other school-fee benefits in state universities and colleges, local universities and colleges, and state-run technical-vocational institutions, alongside student-aid programs such as the Tertiary Education Subsidy.

For low-income families, the cost of tertiary education goes beyond tuition. Books, transport, housing, connectivity, equipment and other study-related expenses can still prevent students from completing a degree or technical-vocational program even when tuition is free.
Watch for the implementing rules, program guidelines and budget allocations that will determine how RA 12325 is applied across higher-education and technical-vocational institutions.

stories.headline: WMO Says El Niño Will Become Very Strong, Persisting Into Early 2027
stories.deck: The global weather agency now sees near-certain persistence through February 2027, strengthening the case for Philippine preparation for drought, heat and water stress even while Habagat can still bring destructive rain.
body: The World Meteorological Organization said El Niño is firmly established and is expected to intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with a nearly 100% likelihood of persisting through February 2027.

PAGASA declared El Niño conditions present in the tropical Pacific on June 9 and said the pattern generally increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall, dry spells and drought across much of the Philippines. It also stressed that western parts of the country can still receive above-normal rainfall during the Southwest Monsoon, especially when tropical cyclones enhance Habagat.

For the Philippines, a stronger and longer-lasting El Niño can increase pressure on agriculture, irrigation, water supply, hydropower and heat-sensitive communities. The risk does not mean every part of the country will be dry at the same time, and it does not remove the threat of intense monsoon or cyclone rainfall.

Watch PAGASA's next ENSO and seasonal climate updates for Philippine-specific rainfall, temperature, dry-spell and drought projections. WMO's global outlook does not replace local forecasts, and impacts will vary by region and month.

stories.headline: Palace Orders Alternative Learning in NCR and 15 Provinces Amid Habagat and Haze
stories.deck: The directive covers public and private educational institutions and took effect immediately, while local executives retained authority over localized class suspensions.
body: Malacañang ordered all public and private educational institutions in Metro Manila and 15 provinces to implement alternative learning modes and learning-continuity measures on September 4.
The directive was contained in Memorandum Circular No. 134 signed by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council.
The order covers Metro Manila, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan, Bulacan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Cavite, Laguna, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro.

The Palace cited anticipated continued heavy rainfall associated with the enhanced southwest monsoon and poor air quality in Metro Manila due to haze from severe forest and peatland fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra, Indonesia.

stories.headline: Alex Eala Powers Into US Open Third Round With Straight-Sets Win
stories.deck: The Filipina No. 17 seed defeated Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-1, 6-4 in New York, booking her first US Open third-round appearance.
body: Alexandra Eala advanced to the third round of the 2026 US Open after defeating Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-1, 6-4 in the women’s singles second round in New York on Thursday, September 3, or early Friday, September 4 in the Philippines.
Eala and Oliynykova had met once previously in 2026, with the Ukrainian winning their Strasbourg Open encounter in three sets. The US Open rematch reversed that result.
Eala’s progress gives Philippine tennis another high-profile Grand Slam result and extends a season in which she has broken several national milestones on the WTA Tour.
Eala will next play in the US Open third round. Her next opponent and match schedule should be confirmed through the official tournament draw and schedule.
